item.title: ALL4ONE#525 McCartney Plays Bass for the Stones, Clapton & Cale at 20, Fleetwood Mac & More
item.description:
This 525th episode of ALL4ONE opens with a run of new 2026 releases from artists with nothing left to prove. Josh Rouse kicks things off with “Museums and Women,” then Paul McCartney delivers “One Night Stand,” one of three previously unreleased songs on the special edition of The Boys of Dungeon Lane, recorded during the album sessions with producer Andrew Watt. The Rolling Stones follow with “Covered in You,” from their 25th album Foreign Tongues, and look who’s playing bass: McCartney himself. Mick Jagger reportedly checked with producer Andrew Watt that Paul’s playing was punk enough for the song, and he nailed it in about ten minutes. Peter Frampton and Sheryl Crow then join voices on “Breaking the Mold,” from Carry the Light, Frampton’s first album of original material in 16 years, co-written and produced with his son Julian. Crow runs through the whole show, from “Redemption Day” with Johnny Cash to “Come On Up to the House” with Willie and Lukas Nelson, before returning with “Freight Train,” the opener of her new seven-song album Pick You Up, a slow, reflective song about feeling alone, even in a crowd.

The americana section brings Ryan Bingham, John Mellencamp, and John Hiatt, then J.J. Cale and Eric Clapton’s “Missing Person.” It’s no coincidence: The Road to Escondido returns on November 20 in an Enhanced Edition for its 20th anniversary, with three unreleased songs from the original sessions, three live tracks, and new liner notes. Neil Young & The Chrome Hearts follow with “Earth Girl,” from Second Song, cut on analog tape at Rick Rubin’s Shangri-La studio in Malibu. The band includes guitarist Micah Nelson, Lukas Nelson’s brother, which closes the circle with the Nelson family. After The Lumineers’ take on “Sugar Mountain” and a run of fresh 2026 tracks from Beck, Jake Bugg, and more, Tyler Ballgame’s “Live It Down” sounds, to our ears at least, like it fell out of the Fleetwood Mac catalog, and that’s our doorway to the finale. The show closes with the Rumours medley, then Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks, Buckingham and Christine McVie, and Stevie Nicks with Tom Petty and The Heartbreakers.
